grammar.summary: 本课以洞穴探险为题材，大量运用定语从句补充说明洞穴特征与探险细节，用被动语态客观叙述洞穴的形成与发现过程，并在篇首出现 It is...that... 强调句型来突出洞穴探险的诱因。

points.title: 强调句型 (Cleft Sentence)
points.explanation: 强调句的结构为 It is/was + 被强调部分 + that/who + 句子其余部分。被强调的可以是主语、宾语或状语。本课开篇用 It is...that... 强调「独处的愿望」和「意外发现的机会」正是吸引人们深入地下的原因，使叙事更具感染力。

examples.en: Perhaps it is the desire for solitude or the chance of making an unexpected discovery that lures people down to the depths of the earth.
examples.cn: 寻求独处的愿望或寻求意外发现的机会的欲望吸引人们来到地下深处。

points.title: 定语从句 (Relative Clauses)
points.explanation: 用关系代词 which/that 引导定语从句修饰先行词（物），which 在从句中可作主语或宾语。本课多次用 which 修饰洞穴特征和具体事物，如 fascination、instincts、waterfall 等，使长句紧凑、信息丰富。

examples.en: For him, caves have the same peculiar fascination which high mountains have for the climber.
examples.cn: 对洞穴探险者来说，洞穴有一种特殊的魅力，就像高山对登山者有特殊魅力一样。

examples.en: They arouse instincts which can only be dimly understood.
examples.cn: 为什么洞空能引发人的那种探险本能，人们对此只能有一种模模糊糊的理解。

examples.en: Suddenly they came to a waterfall which dropped into an underground lake at the bottom of the cave.
examples.cn: 突然，他们来到一道瀑布前，那瀑布奔泻而下，注入洞底一处地下湖里。

points.title: 被动语态 (Passive Voice)
points.explanation: 被动语态 be + 过去分词用于突出动作的承受者或当不必指出执行者时。本课用现在完成时被动语态 has been formed 叙述洞穴由暗流冲刷而成，用 remains to be explored 表达「尚待探索」，客观呈现洞穴的形成与发现过程。

examples.en: This immense chasm has been formed by an underground stream which has tunneled a course through a flaw in the rocks.
examples.cn: 这个深邃的洞穴是由一条地下暗泉冲刷岩石中的缝隙并使之慢慢变大而形成的。

examples.en: Though a number of descents have been made, much of it still remains to be explored.
examples.cn: 自从被发现以后，这个洞成了洞穴探险者的珠穆朗玛峰，人们多次进入洞内探险，但至今尚有不少东西有待勘探。

exercises.q: Perhaps it is the desire for solitude or the chance of making an unexpected discovery ______ lures people down to the depths of the earth.
They arouse instincts ______ can only be dimly understood.
This immense chasm has been formed by an underground stream which has tunneled a course ______ a flaw in the rocks. 句中 has been formed 是什么语态？
用被动语态填空：The cave might never have been discovered ______ (if/had) not the entrance been spotted by the distinguished French pot-holer, Berger.（写出使句子成立的关系词，结合倒装结构）
